In chloroplasts, mostly in the palisade mesophyll cells of leaves.
Tiny pores, mostly on the underside of leaves. They let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out.
Carries water and minerals up from the roots to the leaves. It is made of dead, hollow cells.

Palisade: tall cells packed with chloroplasts, where most photosynthesis happens. Spongy: loosely packed cells with air spaces for gases to diffuse.

front: Five uses of the glucose a plant makes
back: Respiration, storage as starch, cellulose for cell walls, sugars for transport, and proteins (with nitrates from the soil).

front: How do you test a leaf for starch?
back: Boil in water, decolourise in hot ethanol (water bath), rinse, then add iodine. Blue-black = starch.
All the time, day and night, in every living cell.

front: Three factors that affect the rate of photosynthesis
back: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature.

front: How are leaves adapted for photosynthesis?
back: Broad and flat (large surface area for light), thin (short distance for gases), many chloroplasts, stomata, and veins.
